claims.text: Equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi is the Cantor alloy.
The Co-free FeNiCrMn alloy is derived from equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
Solid-solution Co-free FeNiCrMn has a favorable strength–ductility balance.
The strength–ductility balance in Co-free FeNiCrMn is governed by a dynamic transition between dislocation glide and deformation twinning.
Deformation under lower-temperature conditions promotes transient local short-range ordering in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Deformation at higher strain rates promotes transient local short-range ordering in Co-free FeNiCrMn.
Strain-induced local short-range ordering lowers the effective stacking-fault energy.
Reduced stacking-fault energy facilitates the nucleation of deformation twins.
Lower temperature increases the contribution of deformation twinning relative to room-temperature quasi-static loading.
Higher strain rate increases the contribution of deformation twinning relative to room-temperature quasi-static loading.
Deformation twins impede dislocation motion and thereby help maintain high strength.
Deformation twinning supplies additional deformation accommodation that contributes to ductility.
Lower-temperature loading should raise yield strength without a proportional loss of ductility relative to room-temperature quasi-static loading.
Higher-strain-rate loading should raise yield strength without a proportional loss of ductility relative to room-temperature quasi-static loading.
Lower-temperature or higher-strain-rate loading should alter dislocation patterns relative to the baseline.
The proposed mechanism applies only while the alloy remains a solid solution and no phase transition occurs.
Significant thermal softening, adiabatic heating, or melting can mask the proposed effect.
The quantitative influence of strain-induced short-range order on stacking-fault energy and twin nucleation in Co-free FeNiCrMn remains unmeasured.
